name: rm
description: Permanently deletes the given files. There is no trash: a file deleted with rm usually cannot be recovered. By default, rm refuses to delete a directory.

options.description: Deletes directories and everything in them, recursively. -R is the same.
Never asks for confirmation and ignores files that do not exist.
Asks for confirmation before each deletion.
Asks once before deleting more than three files or when deleting recursively.

examples.explanation: Deletes the .tmp files, asking for confirmation for each one.
Deletes the build directory and everything in it.
Deletes a file whose name starts with a dash: “--” marks the end of options.

dangerNote: Deletion is permanent. rm -rf deletes everything without confirmation: always check the path, especially with variables or wildcards (*).
